evals.name: draws-a-project
evals.prompt: Draw the architecture of this project for the README.
evals.expected_output: docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml passes `archgram check`, and <name>.svg is drawn beside it. It has the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker, each backed by a file in src/ and named in the report with it; every node a file backs and every edge carries a source (the file behind it, and for an edge a few words of the line that makes it), each one that `archgram check` finds; a flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres. The prompt asks for no colours, so the drawing keeps archgram's own, though src/styles.css has colours of its own: no theme is written and the report says the project's colours can be asked for. The skill did not ask any question. Each edge in the report has the file and line that makes it, the drawing is no wider than 1,300 px, its spec names the direction archgram chose rather than `auto`, and no browser was started and no screenshot taken: only the finished SVG was opened, with the system's viewer.
expectations: A spec at docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml and <name>.svg beside it exist
The run ran `archgram check` on the final spec, and it passes
The spec is an architecture diagram, not a sequence: it has no `diagram: sequence`, since the prompt asks what the project is made of
The spec has nodes for the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker
Each of those nodes has a source naming its file in src/
Every node a file backs and every edge has a source, an edge's with a few words of the line that makes it; an edge from a node no file backs is sourced at the line that receives it
A flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres
No theme is written (no archgram.theme.json, no resolver) and no build passes --theme-file: the prompt asked for no colours
The report says the colours are archgram's own, and that the project's can be asked for
The SVG is no wider than 1,300 px
Each edge label is a few words, two or three; any longer detail is in a node's note or the report
The final spec names the direction `build` chose (`right` or `down`), not `auto`, and no `shownWidth`: the prompt asks for a README
The run asked the user no question
The report gives each edge with the file and line that makes it, and each cited line holds the code it quotes
No browser was started and no screenshot taken
The finished SVG was opened with the system's viewer (`open`, `xdg-open` or `start`); a run whose attempt was denied counts as having opened it
README.md is left unchanged, and the report offers the line that shows the drawing in it

evals.name: draws-a-sequence
evals.prompt: Draw what happens when someone signs in, step by step, for the README.
evals.expected_output: The request asks for the order of the calls of one request, so the skill draws a sequence, not architecture: docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml has `diagram: sequence`, passes `archgram check`, and <name>.svg is drawn beside it. Its participants are the browser, the API (src/routes/login.ts), the auth service, external (src/auth.ts), the users in Postgres (src/db.ts) and the audit stream in Redis (src/audit.ts), left to right in the order the request reaches them. Its messages follow src/routes/login.ts in the order the code runs: POST /login, verify session and the claims back, find user and the user back, then an `alt` on the password, whose first way records the sign-in in the audit stream as a send that does not wait (`async: true`) and replies with the session, and whose `else` replies 401 with `refused: true`. Each call carries a source with a few words of the line that makes it, which `archgram check` finds. Two to four phases divide the story, each a few words. It has no `direction`, no `flows` and no `still`. The report gives the reader contract, each participant with its file and each message in order with its line. The skill asked no question, started no browser, took no screenshot, and opened only the finished SVG with the system's viewer.
expectations: A spec at docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml with `diagram: sequence`, and <name>.svg beside it, exist
